{{Short description|None}}
{{for|the head coaches after 1993|List of Dallas Stars head coaches}}
{{featured list}}
The [[Minnesota North Stars]] were an American professional [[ice hockey]] team based in [[Bloomington, Minnesota]], a city in the [[United States metropolitan area|U.S. metropolitan statistical area]] of [[Minneapolis–Saint Paul]].<ref name=MSA-pop>{{cite web|author=U.S. Census Bureau |title=Annual Estimates of the Population of Metropolitan and Micropolitan Statistical Areas: April 1, 2000 to July 1, 2006 (CBSA-EST2006-01) |url=https://www.census.gov/population/www/estimates/CBSA-est2006-annual.html |date=July 1, 2006 |access-date=August 31, 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090905050237/http://www.census.gov/population/www/estimates/CBSA-est2006-annual.html |archive-date=September 5, 2009 }}</ref> The team joined the [[1967 NHL expansion|NHL in 1967]] as an [[expansion team]] with five other teams;<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hockey-reference.com/teams|title=Teams Index|publisher=Sports Reference LLC|work=Hockey-Reference.com|access-date=September 5, 2009|archive-date=August 27, 2008|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080827205557/http://hockey-reference.com/teams/|url-status=live}}</ref> the [[Cleveland Barons (NHL)|Cleveland Barons]], another 1967 NHL expansion team, were merged with the North Stars in the [[1978–79 NHL season|1978–79 season]].<ref>{{cite book|last=McFarlane|first=Brian|year=1990|title=100 Years of Hockey|publisher=Summerhill Press|isbn=0-929091-26-4}}</ref> The North Stars played in the [[Stanley Cup Final]] twice: as the [[Prince of Wales Conference]] champions in the [[1980–81 NHL season|1980–81 season]],<ref>{{cite book |editor=McCarthy, Dave |year=2008 |title=The National Hockey League Official Guide & Record Book/2009 |publisher=Dan Diamond Associates |isbn=978-1-894801-14-0}}</ref> and in the [[1990–91 NHL season|1990–91 season]] after winning the [[Clarence S. Campbell Bowl]],<ref name="cscb">{{cite web|url=http://www.nhl.com/trophies/campbell.html |title=Clarence S. Campbell Bowl |publisher=[[National Hockey League]] |access-date=September 5, 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080723230820/http://www.nhl.com/trophies/campbell.html |archive-date=July 23, 2008 }}</ref> but lost in both Finals.<ref name="champs">{{cite web|url=http://www.nhl.com/cup/champs.html |title=Stanley Cup Champions and Finalists |publisher=[[National Hockey League]] |access-date=September 5, 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090629213230/http://www.nhl.com/cup/champs.html |archive-date=June 29, 2009 }}</ref> The North Stars played their home games at the [[Met Center]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.startribune.com/sports/wild/16362601.html|title=Rising in the North: NHL comes to Minnesota|work=[[Star Tribune]]|author=Youngblood, Kent|date=March 7, 2008|access-date=September 5, 2009|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080610185158/http://www.startribune.com/sports/wild/16362601.html|archive-date=June 10, 2008}}</ref> The team relocated to [[Dallas]], Texas in 1993, after former owner [[Norman Green]] announced that he was moving the team to Dallas's [[Reunion Arena]] in search of a better economic situation,<ref>{{cite magazine|url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/vault/article/magazine/MAG1138154/1/index.htm|title=Norm Green is reviled in Minnesota for his decision to move the North Stars south|publisher=[[Time Warner]]|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]|date=April 19, 1993|access-date=August 31, 2009|author=Montville, Leigh|archive-date=September 18, 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090918212121/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/vault/article/magazine/MAG1138154/1/index.htm|url-status=dead}}</ref> and are now known as the [[Dallas Stars]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cbssports.com/nhl/teams/history/DAL|title=Dallas Stars History|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|work=[[CBS Sports]]|access-date=August 31, 2009|archive-date=October 11, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121011001105/http://www.cbssports.com/nhl/teams/history/DAL|url-status=live}}</ref> The North Stars played in the [[Norris Division]] of the [[Clarence Campbell Conference]] in the [[National Hockey League]] (NHL) in [[1992–93 Minnesota North Stars season|their last season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hockey-reference.com/teams/DAL|title=Dallas Stars|publisher=Sports Reference LLC|work=Hockey-Reference.com|access-date=August 31, 2009|archive-date=September 15, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110915070607/http://www.hockey-reference.com/teams/DAL/|url-status=live}}</ref> There were 16 [[head coach]]es for the North Stars team.<ref name="hr">{{cite web|url=https://www.hockey-reference.com/teams/DAL/coaches.html|title=Dallas Stars Coach Register|publisher=Sports Reference LLC|work=Hockey-Reference.com|access-date=August 31, 2009|archive-date=November 20, 2008|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081120194627/http://www.hockey-reference.com/teams/DAL/coaches.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

The North Stars' first head coach and [[general manager]] was [[Wren Blair]], who coached for the first three seasons, and was the [[List of Minnesota North Stars general managers|North Stars' general manager]] until 1974; [[Jack Gordon (ice hockey)|Jack Gordon]], [[Lou Nanne]], and [[Bob Gainey]] were also the general manager of the North Stars during their tenures as head coach.<ref name="ds">{{cite web|url=http://stars.nhl.com/ext/pdf/DAL0809MediaGuide.pdf|title=2008-2009 Media Guide|publisher=[[National Hockey League]] and the [[Dallas Stars]]|access-date=September 5, 2009|page=264|archive-date=December 21, 2008|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081221020826/http://stars.nhl.com/ext/pdf/DAL0809MediaGuide.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref> Nine of the first twelve North Stars head coaches lasted less than two complete seasons, while ten of the first twelve head coaches have spent their entire NHL head coaching careers with the North Stars. Gordon was the first North Stars head coach to have coached more than two complete seasons, with four.<ref name="hr"/>

Several head coaches have had multiple tenures with the North Stars. [[Glen Sonmor]] served three terms as North Stars head coach. He is the North Stars' all-time leader for the most regular-season games coached, regular-season game wins, regular-season [[Point (ice hockey)|points]], playoff games coached, and playoff-game wins. Sonmor's first term lasted five seasons, the longest duration for one North Stars head coach term; his last term lasted two games, which was the shortest tenure.<ref name="hr"/> Blair, Gordon and [[Charlie Burns]] each served two terms as the North Stars' head coach.<ref name="ds"/> None of their second terms were winning seasons.<ref name="hr"/>

Burns, [[Ted Harris (ice hockey)|Ted Harris]], [[Parker MacDonald]], Nanne, and [[Murray Oliver]] had once [[List of Minnesota North Stars players|played for the North Stars]];<ref>{{cite web|url=http://stars.nhl.com/ext/pdf/DAL0809MediaGuide.pdf|title=2008-2009 Media Guide|publisher=[[National Hockey League]] and the [[Dallas Stars]]|access-date=September 5, 2009|page=266|archive-date=December 21, 2008|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081221020826/http://stars.nhl.com/ext/pdf/DAL0809MediaGuide.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref> Burns is the only person to have been a [[player-coach]] for the North Stars, having done so in the [[1969–70 NHL season|1969–70 season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.legendsofhockey.net/LegendsOfHockey/jsp/SearchPlayer.jsp?player=12156|title=Charlie Frederick Burns|publisher=[[Hockey Hall of Fame]]|access-date=September 5, 2009|archive-date=June 17, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110617105849/http://www.legendsofhockey.net/LegendsOfHockey/jsp/SearchPlayer.jsp?player=12156|url-status=live}}</ref> [[Miracle on Ice|1980 U.S. Olympic "Miracle on Ice"]] coach [[Herb Brooks]], who coached the North Stars in the [[1987–88 NHL season|1987–88 season]], is the only North Stars head coach to have been elected to the [[Hockey Hall of Fame]] as a [[List of members of the Hockey Hall of Fame#Builders|builder]];<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hhof.com/legendsofhockey/html/ind06Brooks.htm|title=Herb Brooks - Builders Category|publisher=[[Hockey Hall of Fame]]|access-date=September 6, 2009|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110604135356/http://www.hhof.com/legendsofhockey/html/ind06Brooks.htm|archive-date=June 4, 2011}}</ref> [[Harry Howell (ice hockey)|Harry Howell]] and Gainey were inducted as [[List of members of the Hockey Hall of Fame#Players|players]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.legendsofhockey.net/LegendsOfHockey/jsp/LegendsMember.jsp?mem=p197901&type=Player&page=bio&list=ByName#photo|title=Players - Harry Howell|publisher=[[Hockey Hall of Fame]]|access-date=September 6, 2009|archive-date=June 17, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110617105908/http://www.legendsofhockey.net/LegendsOfHockey/jsp/LegendsMember.jsp?mem=p197901&type=Player&page=bio&list=ByName#photo|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.legendsofhockey.net/LegendsOfHockey/jsp/LegendsMember.jsp?mem=p199203&type=Player&page=bio&list=ByName#photo|title=Players - Bob Gainey|publisher=[[Hockey Hall of Fame]]|access-date=September 6, 2009|archive-date=June 17, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110617105949/http://www.legendsofhockey.net/LegendsOfHockey/jsp/LegendsMember.jsp?mem=p199203&type=Player&page=bio&list=ByName#photo|url-status=live}}</ref> Sonmor and Gainey are the only head coaches to reach the Stanley Cup Final with the North Stars, in the [[1981 Stanley Cup Final|1981]] and [[1991 Stanley Cup Final|1991 Finals]] respectively.<ref name="champs"/> Gainey was the last head coach of the North Stars; he coached the franchise until the [[1995–96 NHL season|1995–96 season]].<ref name="hr"/>
